newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to favour small savers in ENI sale.
newsitem.headline: Italy to favour small savers in ENI sale.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is likely to offer small investors a discount on the public offer price for the second tranche sale of energy giant ENI next month.
This would be the first time small savers have been offered such a discount in the country's privatisation programme.
At the same time, the Treasury will offer a "loyalty" premium of a one-for-10 bonus share for small investors who hold on to their shares for at least one year.
The details were published in an outline prospectus for the Eni share sale published in financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore.
Italian stock market authority Consob on Wednesday approved the prospectus for the public offering which is set to start on October 21 and end on October 25.
The amount of the second tranche of shares to be offered has not been yet set but Eni has said the state, which now holds 85 percent of shares, will still retain control of the group.

Details of the second tranche amount will be announced on October 7. The first tranche of 15 percent of ENI shares was floated at 5,250 lire a share late last year. The shares trade in Milan, London and New York.
The maximum placement price and the eventual discount to small investors will be fixed on October 20 and the official public offer price announced on October 27.
